answer: A per-agent stake channel is one concrete Sybil barrier. Each identity must lock a bond scaling with the influence it seeks, and the protocol samples a random deliberation vertex each round to check that the agent's output diverges from its own prior answers. A clone emits an echo of the original, so the divergence test flags correlated clusters and merges them. Honest agents forge their bond once and reuse it; an attacker spinning up ten thousand fakes must post ten thousand real stakes they forfeit on detection, turning cheap identity inflation into a large sunk cost.
